world: ⭐⭐⭐ A UNREADABLE, AND THE COMPARISON WAS BIASED BEFORE IT WAS UNREADABLE. R716's NEXT line proposed splitting the provenance share by k — but the share IS m/k, so the split conditions on the statistic's own DENOMINATOR, and the groups do not share a support: k=4 admits {0,¼,½,¾,1} and k=2 admits {0,½,1}. ⭐ At the same match count m=1 the share is 0.2500 at k=4 and 0.5000 at k=2, so identical counts FORCE a higher share in the smaller-k group — the bias has a known SIGN and it pushes the small group UP. ⭐⭐ THE OBSERVED DIFFERENCE RUNS AGAINST IT: small minus big is -0.0131 on the share and -0.1052 on the count, both NEGATIVE. ⛔ BUT NONE OF IT IS READABLE: the MDE at the true 44/942 imbalance is 0.080 — 2.0× R716's even-split 0.040 — against an observed |difference| of 0.0131. ⭐ SO R716's OWN CAUTION WAS RIGHT AND ITS QUESTION IS STILL UNANSWERABLE: an even-split MDE does not carry over to a group of 44, and this is the second time in three rounds that computing the resolution first turned a proposed comparison into a bound. ⚠ AND THE SHAM ESTABLISHES LESS THAN IT LOOKS: 0 of 6 sweep cells survive their own null — INCLUDING the k-split cells — so the id-parity sham landing inside the null at -0.0213 does NOT show that the k-split is the ingredient. It shows that NO split at this imbalance is readable, which is weaker and different. ⚠ AND THE BIAS CANNOT BE ANALYSED AWAY: every share with k in its denominator inherits it; only the raw count avoids it, and R716 measured the count's MDE as 5–7× worse. ⚠ UNIT GAP: instrument unit is A CORE INSTANCE, claim unit is WHETHER THE k-GROUPS DIFFER IN PROVENANCE.
